title: WHY PIGEONS BOB THEIR HEADS WHILE WALKING

narration_timeline.text: Why does this city pigeon move its head in little jerks as it walks?
narration_timeline.scene: Single pigeon walking on city pavement.

narration_timeline.text: Rock pigeons share ledges and sidewalks with people, and their steps reveal a surprising trick.
On pavement or rooftops, the body steps forward while the head briefly holds still, then catches up.
narration_timeline.scene: Pigeons walking on a path and on rooftop courtship footage.

narration_timeline.text: When a pigeon rests, that head movement disappears because its body is no longer walking.
narration_timeline.scene: Pigeon visibly resting on gravel, no claim of movement.

narration_timeline.text: But walking is only part of city life: pigeons also peck at the ground, gather to bathe and preen.
narration_timeline.scene: Pigeon pecking at city ground, followed by group bathing in shallow water; inspect both exact windows.

narration_timeline.text: Once they move again, the familiar bob returns across paths and waterside grass.
narration_timeline.scene: Pigeons walking on grass and group on path, two sources.
